answer.text: Unlimited potential loss (for calls) or significant loss (for puts) and limited premium gain

explanation.text: The Logic: An option writer (seller) is obliged to honour the contract if the buyer exercises. In exchange for receiving the premium up front (the writer's maximum gain), the writer takes on the opposite payoff of the buyer: for a short call the loss rises with the underlying price and is theoretically unlimited; for a short put the loss can be very large (capped only by the underlying going to zero, less premium received). The asymmetric payoff — limited gain (premium), large or unlimited loss — is the defining risk profile of writing options. The Trap: 'No obligation' and 'no risk' confuse the writer's position with the buyer's; only the buyer has the right but not the obligation. 'Infinite upside' is the long-call buyer's profile, not the writer's. Note: The cited NISM Series XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook pages checked only state that the writer has the obligation to honour the contract if the buyer exercises; the specific loss-profile claim (unlimited for calls, large for puts, limited premium gain) is not in those pages. The framing above is presented as general options-payoff knowledge rather than as a workbook citation.
